Given that $R$ is the type III region shown above, 
${∭}_{R}xz\,\text{d}V=$
question.worked_solution:
For a type III region $R$ with projection $D$ onto the $xz$-plane, the triple integral of a continuous function $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ is given by

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

We consider the region $R$ as a type III region enclosed between the back surface $y={u}_{1}(x,z)=1$ and the front surface $y={u}_{2}(x,z)=3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/b176bcf502a0801eae2bf470dfe4bf92852a34b06675fd74be78b30ccb4f6469.png)

So, the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,1\le y\le 3\}.
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ as a type I *plane* region in the $xz$-plane with the upper curve

$$
z=1-{x}^{2}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/eb054b5f1567aa2c56842d79133fbbefc41a8b40730c688381d88e3ef06ccab7.png)

Hence, $D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le 1-{x}^{2}\}.$

Therefore, we write the triple integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}xz\,\text{d}V & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{1}^{3}xz\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}[{\int }_{1}^{3}xz\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}xz[y]_{y=1}^{y=3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{x}^{2}}2xz\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
